title: Local capacity and mobility cells carry different political-context patterns without a simple trust or action gradient
source_unit: 2024 Cooperative Election Study common-content post-election respondent with county FIPS, assigned to 2023 county CBP health-establishment and ACS zero-vehicle context cell
geography: United States; 620 counties with at least 100,000 residents and valid 2020/2023 population estimates

observations.period: 2024; CES county-keyed political context; high health capacity / high zero-vehicle share

denominator.unit: CES respondents; 188 counties; population frame counties >=100,000

median_population_change_pct.unit: percent county population change, 2020–2023; median within capacity cell

federal_trust.unit: percent trusting federal government a great deal or fair amount; commonpostweight

state_trust.unit: percent trusting state government a great deal or fair amount; commonpostweight

civic_action.unit: percent reporting at least one selected civic action; commonpostweight

reported_voted.unit: percent reporting definitely voted in November 2024; commonpostweight

observations.method: Weighted descriptive CES common-content comparison after county-keyed assignment to CBP health-establishment/zero-vehicle four cells; health cut 28.312 establishments per 10,000 and zero-vehicle cut 5.606 percent are unweighted medians within the >=100,000-population frame.
observations.uncertainty: No complex-survey standard errors or county-representative estimates; CES county FIPS supplies context but respondents are not a county probability sample, and the cell does not measure respondent-level capacity exposure.
observations.subgroup: CES respondents in the high health capacity / high zero-vehicle share capacity/mobility context cell.
observations.counterinterpretation: Trust, action, and reported voting can reflect party identity, county composition, selection, local growth, and question universe; a capacity cell is not a service-use, belonging, or causal exposure measure.

related_sources.claim: CES 2024 common-content public data supply county FIPS, trust, civic-action, vote, and commonpostweight fields.
2023 CBP health/social-assistance establishment counts used for capacity cell assignment.
2023 ACS zero-vehicle-household counts used for mobility cell assignment.
Reproduction script for county capacity-cell assignment, valid universes, and weighted endpoints.

boundary: This is a same-county contextual comparison, not a same-respondent causal exposure. It does not establish that local business/service capacity or vehicle constraints caused trust, civic action, or voting; it does not measure service destination, use, belonging, attribution, or political meaning. CES and county administrative/ACS layers retain separate denominators and uncertainty.
